alcohol dehydrogenases (ADH) are enzymes that play important roles in the metabolism of ethanol and other alcohols.

alcohol dehydrogenases are involved in the development of cancer and their activities in cancer tissues are different in comparison with healthy tissues, what may be important in the diagnostics of cancer diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the activity of AD and ALDH in cancer tissues and serum of cancer patients.
the role of alcohol dehydrogenases and aldehyde dehyrdrogenases in the development of cancer.
the role of ADH and ALDH in the carcinogenesis and cancer diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the activity of AD, and in particular ADH2 and ADH3, in cancerous tissues is higher than in normal ones.

the changes in the activities of alcohol dehydrogenases in the cancer diseases may be a result of increased ethanol oxidation, but also a factor of carcinogenesis by the formation of acetaldehyde from ethanol and disorders of the metabolism of some biolologically important substances.

the activity of ADHD and ALDH isoenzymes is a factor intensifying the carcinogenesis by increased ability to acetylaldehyde formation from ethanol, and disorders in metabolism some biologically important substance (e.g. vitamin A).

ADH and ALDH are the key enzymes in the carcinogenesis process.
the activity of AD, ADH and ALDH isoenzymes may be useful for the diagnosis of different cancers.
